documents.title: Chronic Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Urology's October letter came in December: PVR 120 mL, continue tamsulosin, double voiding. Reviewed with him.
No UTIs this winter. Up 1-2 times a night.
Sugars fine, no lows. Home BP at goal.
Exam: BP/HR per flowsheet. Heart and lungs unremarkable. Feet normal.
A/P: T2DM - A1c today. HTN - continue lisinopril. BPH - tamsulosin, urology as needed. Statin continued.
Next visit May for a check, July for yearly labs.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt cancelling tomorrow 10:40, will be out of town. Rebooked for July with yearly labs.

documents.title: Office Visit: Groin Bulge, Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Noticed a bulge in the right groin about 6-8 weeks ago, after hauling bags of mulch. Aches at the end of the day, goes away lying down. No vomiting, bowels normal.
Also due for diabetes labs.
Exam: standing, soft reducible bulge right inguinal region with cough impulse, nontender. Left side normal. Testes normal.
Heart regular, lungs clear, feet intact with normal sensation.
A/P
1. Right inguinal hernia, reducible, symptomatic. Referral to general surgery for elective repair. Reviewed incarceration warning signs.
2. T2DM / HTN / statin: A1c, CMP, lipids, urine albumin today. No med changes.
3. BPH on tamsulosin: stable. Flagged to the surgeon that he has prostate enlargement on tamsulosin.

documents.title: Lab Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, lipids, A1c and urine albumin back. Nothing new; liver tests normal on the statin. Released with comment.

documents.title: Hernia surgery date
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the surgeon last week. They are doing the hernia repair on Monday October 9, as an outpatient. Do they need anything from you?

documents.title: RE: Hernia surgery date
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Your July labs and exam are recent, so they can use those. If they send a pre-op form we will fill it out. Keep taking your tamsulosin up to the surgery unless they tell you otherwise.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Exam Letter
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual diabetic eye evaluation 08/24/2023 (dilated). Visual acuity stable 20/25 each eye. No retinopathy, no edema at the macula. See again in one year. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Hernia repair booked for 10/9 with the outside surgeon.
Still independent, walking daily though the knee is slowing him down; ortho has started to talk about a replacement.
No falls. Hearing fine. Vision: optometry August, no retinopathy.
Brief cognitive screen normal. PHQ-2 negative.
Vaccines: high-dose flu and RSV today, one in each arm. COVID updated formula next month.
Preventive: colonoscopy 2017 normal; next due 2027, will revisit given age.
Follow-up December.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 10/11/2023 18:50

CC: no urine output for about 8 hours with severe low abdominal pain.
HPI: 71M with BPH, seen by urology in April and October of last year, who had an elective inguinal hernia repair two days ago. Over the past year he has had progressive trouble voiding: weak stream, nighttime voiding, a feeling of not emptying. Since this morning he has not been able to pass urine at all and the lower belly pain is now severe.
PMH: BPH, type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Recent right inguinal herniorrhaphy (10/09).
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, social drinker.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 88. Uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Abdomen distended with suprapubic tenderness. Right groin incision clean and dry. DRE: enlarged firm prostate, not tender.
Bedside bladder ultrasound: markedly distended bladder, estimated 600 mL.

Course: urethral catheter placed without difficulty with prompt relief.
Impression: acute urinary retention after hernia repair, underlying BPH.
Disposition: home with indwelling catheter and leg bag; continue tamsulosin; urology office for voiding trial in about one week. Return for fever, catheter blockage or bleeding.

Record received by fax 10/13/2023.

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I ended up in the ER last night. Couldn't pee at all after the hernia surgery. They put a catheter in and I have to keep it until urology sees me next Wednesday. Feeling much better, just a nuisance.

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, but glad you got relief. That happens sometimes after surgery when the prostate is already enlarged. Keep the bag below your bladder, drink normally, and call us for fever, chills, or if it stops draining. Let me know how the urology visit goes.

documents.title: Catheter out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Urology took the catheter out yesterday and I passed their test, peed on my own before I left. Back to normal.

documents.title: RE: Catheter out
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Great news, thanks for the update. We'll add a note to your chart. We haven't received anything from urology about yesterday; if they gave you paperwork, you can send us a photo.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2023-24 COVID vaccine IM left deltoid. Screening negative. Observed, no reaction. Voiding normally since catheter removal per pt.

documents.title: Office Visit: Orthostatic Lightheadedness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: lightheaded on standing.
HPI: For roughly two months, mostly when he gets up out of a chair, he feels lightheaded for several seconds; sometimes the room seems to swim and his vision blurs briefly. Passes if he stands still. No falls, no syncope, no chest pain. Had the retention episode in October after the hernia repair; voiding fine since the catheter came out.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4 (takes it in the morning), atorvastatin 20.

Exam: seated BP 145/85, HR 78. After 3 minutes standing BP 120/70, HR 88. Mildly symptomatic on standing.
Rest of exam unremarkable: heart regular, no murmur, lungs clear, neuro nonfocal, gait steady.

Labs (drawn this morning, resulted before he left): A1c 7.2, creatinine 1.1, Na 140, K 4.2.

A/P
1. Orthostatic hypotension, symptomatic. Talked about getting up in stages, sitting on the edge of the bed first, drinking enough through the day, and moving the tamsulosin to bedtime.
2. T2DM: A1c 7.2, continue metformin.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril.
4. BPH s/p retention: continue tamsulosin.
Call if a fall or fainting. Follow up in the spring.

documents.title: Knee replacement
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ortho wants to do my right knee replacement on April 22. They need a medical clearance from you within 30 days of surgery. Can I book that?

documents.title: RE: Knee replacement
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Booked you for March 12 at 9:00 for the pre-op visit with labs and an EKG. Please bring the surgeon's form.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate in the 70s. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T wave abnormality. No prior for comparison.

documents.title: Preoperative Medical Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVALUATION
Procedure: right total knee arthroplasty, outside orthopedics, planned 4/22/2024.
Functional capacity: walks 1-2 miles, climbs two flights without chest pain or dyspnea (limited by knee, not breath). No cardiac history.
Problems: T2DM on metformin; HTN on lisinopril; BPH on tamsulosin with acute retention after hernia repair in Oct 2023; orthostatic hypotension on standing (counseled Dec, now taking tamsulosin at night, fewer spells). Hernia repaired in October, problem list updated.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Right knee crepitus, varus.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm.
Labs today: CBC, BMP, A1c.
Assessment: acceptable risk for planned orthopedic surgery.
Recommendations to the surgical team:
- Hold metformin the morning of surgery; resume when eating.
- Hold lisinopril the morning of surgery.
- Continue tamsulosin, including the night before. History of postoperative urinary retention: please monitor voiding before discharge.
- Get up slowly with PT given orthostatic symptoms.
Form completed and faxed with ECG and labs once resulted.

documents.title: Pre-op Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC normal, BMP normal, A1c 7.0. Faxed to orthopedics with the clearance form.

documents.title: Operative Report: Right Total Knee Arthroplasty
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 04/22/2024
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: primary osteoarthritis, right knee.
Procedure: right total knee arthroplasty, cemented.
Anesthesia: spinal with adductor canal block.
Findings: tricompartmental degenerative change, worst medially.
Estimated blood loss: minimal. No complications. Tourniquet used.
Disposition: PACU, then home the same afternoon per the outpatient joint pathway after PT clearance.
Allergies: NKDA.
Received 06/25/2024 after records request.

events.reason: unable to void after knee surgery

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Date of service 04/23/2024, arrival 03:10

Chief complaint: lower abdominal pain, cannot urinate.
HPI: 72-year-old man with recurrent BPH and a prior episode of acute urinary retention in October 2023, who had a right total knee replacement about 18 hours ago and went home the same day. Has not been able to void since the surgery; lower abdominal discomfort building through the night.
PMH: BPH, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Right TKA 04/22/2024.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 165/90, HR 102. In obvious distress. Abdomen distended and tender over the suprapubic area. Right knee dressing clean, dry, intact.
Urethral catheterization attempted by nursing, unable to pass.
Portable bladder ultrasound: approximately 750 mL.

Course: urology on call came in and placed a coude catheter with return of urine and relief of pain. Heart rate and pressure settled.
Impression: acute urinary retention after total knee arthroplasty, BPH.
Disposition: discharged with indwelling catheter, continue tamsulosin, urology clinic voiding trial in one week.

Faxed to PCP 04/26/2024.

documents.title: Patient Update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called for pt. Knee surgery Monday went fine, but he went back to the ER early Tuesday unable to urinate; urology placed a catheter. He has a voiding trial next Tuesday. No fever, catheter draining. Doing PT at home. Booked post-op visit 5/7. Reviewed catheter care and when to call.

documents.title: Post-op and Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from R TKA. Second episode of acute urinary retention the night after surgery; urology put in a coude catheter in the ED. Voiding trial at urology 4/30, passed per pt, catheter out, voiding on his own. No urology note yet.
Knee: doing home PT, using a cane, pain controlled per ortho plan.
No fever, no dysuria. No lightheadedness lately.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Incision healing, no redness. Calf soft. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable.
A/P
1. S/p R TKA: per ortho; problem list updated.
2. Recurrent acute urinary retention with BPH: continue tamsulosin. Advised to raise this with urology at follow-up.
3. T2DM/HTN: BMP today. Back on all usual meds.
Will request the operative note.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second request to orthopedics for the 4/22 operative report. They say it was never sent. Will fax this week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Knee is a different leg now, off the cane, walking again.
Op note finally arrived 6/25: cemented R TKA, uncomplicated.
Voiding: weak stream and nocturia as before, no retention since April. Tamsulosin at bedtime. Not getting the orthostatic spells much.
DM: no lows. HTN: home readings 120s-130s.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet: normal pulses and sensation.
Plan: A1c, CMP, lipids, urine albumin. Continue current meds. AWV in September.

documents.title: Lab Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c a bit higher than the spring; he was less active around the knee surgery. Kidney function normal, lipids at goal, urine albumin normal. Continue metformin, recheck in January.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Exam Letter
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 08/15/2024. Acuity 20/30 OD, 20/25 OS. Fundi: no diabetic retinopathy OU. Recheck 12 months. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly wellness review. Back to walking after the knee replacement, tutors a neighbor's kid in algebra once a week.
Falls: none. Gets up slowly. Uses a night light for bathroom trips.
Cognition: brief screen normal. PHQ-2 1 (a little low after surgery in the spring, better now).
Vision: optometry August, no retinopathy.
Vaccines: high-dose flu today. COVID shot at a nurse visit late October. RSV done 2023. PCV20 2021. Shingrix 2019.
Advance directive on file.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE
Visit 10/14/2024

Chief complaint: severe lower abdominal pain, unable to pass urine for 24 hours.
HPI: Third presentation for retention. Over the last six months he has had increasing difficulty starting his stream, a weak stream, and getting up at night. For the past day he has passed essentially nothing and now has severe suprapubic pain.
PMH: BPH, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, s/p right TKA.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: abdomen distended, tender suprapubically. DRE: enlarged, firm, nontender prostate.
Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 18.
Bladder scan: 300 mL.

Course: catheter placed, urine drained with relief.
Assessment: recurrent urinary retention, BPH.
Plan: home with catheter; urology for voiding trial.

Copy sent to primary care 11/20/2024 on request.

documents.title: ED Visit Report
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called: in the ER yesterday morning, couldn't urinate for a whole day, catheter placed again. Urology voiding trial set for next Monday. No fever, draining clear. Booked to see PCP next Tuesday. Asked ER for the record.

documents.title: Post-ED Visit: Urinary Retention
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Third retention episode, this time with no surgery or obvious trigger. Catheter in the ED 10/14; voiding trial at urology yesterday, passed, voiding on his own since. Stream still slow. No dysuria, no fever.
The ED record has not come yet; he says his kidney numbers were 'ok.'
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, nontender, bladder not palpable.
UA dip negative.
A/P: recurrent urinary retention with BPH. Continue tamsulosin. He will follow up with urology. Return precautions reviewed: can't void for more than a few hours, go in.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 Moderna COVID vaccine IM right deltoid. Tolerated. Remained 15 minutes without problems.
